bypass.e: From Middle English *bypassen, *bipassen (suggested by past participle by-past, bipast), equivalent to by- + pass.
bypass.g: A road that passes around something, such as a residential area or business district.

bypath.e: From Middle English bypath; by surface analysis, by + path.
bypath.g: An unfrequented path; an indirect route; a byway.

bystander.g: A person who, although present at some event, does not take part in it; an observer, witness, or spectator.

byway.e: From Middle English bywey, equivalent to by- + way.
byway.g: A road or track not following a main route; a secondary or minor road or path.

byword.e: From Middle English byword, byworde (“proverb”), from Old English bīword, bīwyrd, bīwyrde (“proverb, household word", also "adverb”), from Proto-West Germanic *bīwurdī, equivalent to by- + word.
byword.g: A proverb or proverbial expression, common saying; a frequently used word or phrase.
